## Design

### 2026-10-06 – Started working on a standard 60% keyboard, It will use a raspberry pi pico for it's microcontroller. Spend the first time getting used to kicad again, as i haven't worked on it since blueprint. Set u

**2h**

Started working on a standard 60% keyboard, It will use a raspberry pi pico for it's microcontroller. Spend the first time getting used to kicad again, as i haven't worked on it since blueprint. Set up kicad libraries, drew out the schematic and wired the PCB.

![obraz](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6DC9XH6unLhj3m8pRmeiSqGtn0QZ0deu/a7bf2ebc63eafc4ec53e7d6b640973fa2d2f3e5dd7c065177ce8d2caf24d0591.png)

![obraz](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6DC9XH6unLhj3m8pRmeiSqGtn0QZ0deu/0e2877fab3d6089f17c13c99cd85463959d60f4d2bd09095e348a5207412852f.png)

I am yet to connected the MCU either in the schematic or the pcb, i'm leaving that for tommorow.

### 2026-10-07 – Oct. 7th. Started by picking out the exact MCU i want to use, i ultimately landed on kb2040 because it met most of my requirements, is available relatively cheap in my country, and has usb C. I rework

**4h**

Oct. 7th. Started by picking out the exact MCU i want to use, i ultimately landed on kb2040 because it met most of my requirements, is available relatively cheap in my country, and has usb C. I reworked the matrix to fit the 18 GPIO pins of the kb2040

![obraz](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6DC9XH6unLhj3m8pRmeiSqGtn0QZ0deu/51f00ba17ef80edf10cab58d7e485cbf3ca4ce70934befbaa9419393423e13ce.png)

Then i played around with multiple ideas on where to put the MCU on the board. In the end, i landed with this design of a pocket in the top edge. I feel this will be the most comfortable for me to plug my cable in.

![obraz](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6DC9XH6unLhj3m8pRmeiSqGtn0QZ0deu/0d26b363d3575c59346ee21bab06435606f13b6308cc9395c43fcf54e5f9c658.png)

Then, i wanted to start routing! But... kicad started showing me this error.

![obraz](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6DC9XH6unLhj3m8pRmeiSqGtn0QZ0deu/8edb41dbd5cd6bf2e5ed1b1d2e7ea2d69cabfcc18a6c9c49c8aa12c17de100b7.png)

I was completly lost! I googled around, and i found out the file can be corrupted. I checked the file and it had the correct size. I was truly lost, and then i thought to check the file with an online hex editor. It showed me the cause. Even though the file was still the old size, it was filled with zeroes.

![obraz](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6DC9XH6unLhj3m8pRmeiSqGtn0QZ0deu/b0e3c4feb4babd6efaaa988db50c3f264b76edad38e8a0e08d24f6610727544d.png)

I recovered from kicad history snapshots afterwise. Routing also took me a good while. I haven't done it in a while, and i tried my absolute hardest for it to not be a mess.

![obraz](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/6DC9XH6unLhj3m8pRmeiSqGtn0QZ0deu/c83daa75fc2906c642ee12401f910612b8bc8cb8fb06c2ae14cadfca02f3f67f.png)

For tomorrow, i'm thinking of adding a small oled screen. After that, i'll get started working on the case-cad and firmware, so i'm ready for the building part!

I started around 5 PM polish time today, and adjusting for food breaks and all, i think it's fair to say i worked for 4 hours on this session.
